## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

This fixes the order of the migration.

During recreation, it tried to create the statistics table before the meta table, this will of course fail because of key constraints.

This PR adjusts the migration. First handling meta, next handling statistics.

As it is possible that a table has been dropped on the user end, during a failed migration, already. It drops conditionally, after which it will create. This will be able to resume/fix migrations on failed beta's as well.

Tested against SQLite and MySQL (including having them in broken states).

review_comments:
Hi @frenck, unfortunately this still gave some errors on my system:
```
psycopg2.errors.DependentObjectsStillExist: cannot drop table statistics_meta because other objects depend on it
DETAIL:  constraint statistics_metadata_id_fkey on table statistics depends on table statistics_meta
HINT:  Use DROP ... CASCADE to drop the dependent objects too.
```

Fixed it by dropping the tables together using drop_all:
```python
    elif new_version == 18:
        # Recreate the statistics and statisticsmeta tables
        if sqlalchemy.inspect(engine).has_table(StatisticsMeta.__tablename__):
            Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine, tables=[StatisticsMeta.__table__, Statistics.__table__])

        StatisticsMeta.__table__.create(engine)
        Statistics.__table__.create(engine)
```
Nice! Thanks I was working on it on #52453
